function: Over-the-air FL aggregation: AAV downlink broadcast power, device uplink AirComp power and denoising factors, jointly with AAV deployment and sensing batch size, minimizing the optimality-gap bound (p. 7).
system: AAVs (K = 3-4) and ISAC devices (15 per AAV) with scalar single-antenna channels, LoS free-space air-to-ground links, 100 m altitude, no RIS; band not stated (pp. 4, 11).
method: Federated averaging with analog over-the-air aggregation; supervised local training of ridge regression, CNN, ResNet-18; transceiver and deployment optimized by AO, game, QCQP, SCA, sum-of-ratios (pp. 4, 11, 15).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space LoS path loss with phase term and inter-cell interference; learning data: synthetic Gaussian (ridge regression), MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, CIFAR-100 (pp. 4, 11, 13, 15).
test_conditions: Training and testing in one simulated 600 m x 600 m area (3-4 AAVs, 15 devices each); separate runs per energy budget, data distribution, tiers, phase error (pp. 11-15).
baselines: Round-unaware error minimization via [9], truncated channel inversion as in [22], equal power transmission, static AAV, error-free FedAvg; tier weights without overfitting mitigation [42], average weighting (pp. 12, 15).
metrics: Maximum optimality gap (ridge regression), test accuracy (image recognition), objective Γ convergence, optimized powers, AAV positions and sample sizes (pp. 12-15).
complexity: Algorithm 1: O(R[R1K(T+1)^3.5 + R2(KMT+1)^3.5 + R3(2KT+K^2MT+1)^3.5 + R4K(MT+T)^3.5]) with IPM O(J^3.5) per subproblem (p. 10).
openness: none: no code or channel data released; Baidu link only for supplementary proofs (p. 6); learning datasets MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, CIFAR-100 are public (pp. 13, 15).
q1_support: p. 4: "free-space path loss model is utilized to obtain the channel variables". Custom LoS free-space air-to-ground simulator (eq. 4); no 3GPP TR 38.901/38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "maximum optimality gap versus energy budget of ISAC devices"; p. 15: "with the increasing of Δεmax, the trained models still achieve similar test accuracies". Each setting is a separate training run in the same simulated area; the phase-error study is a CSI-error sweep. No trained model is tested in an unseen condition.
q3_support: p. 12: "the uplink transmission power is controlled via truncated channel inversion as in [22]"; p. 12: "all ISAC devices transmit with equal power under the energy budget constraint"; p. 14: "JSCC-Air-Fed outperforms round-unaware error minimization, truncated channel inversion, equal power transmission, and static AAV by 4.44%, 6.93%, 10.47%, and 12.55%". Earlier published aggregation designs ([22]; round-unaware error minimization via [9]) and a fixed equal-power configuration, compared on test accuracy and optimality gap.
q4_support: p. 10: "the total complexity of Algorithm 1 is O(R[R1 K(T + 1)^3.5 + R2 (KMT + 1)^3.5 + R3 (2KT + K^2 MT + 1)^3.5 + R4 K(MT + T)^3.5])". Order of complexity of the transceiver, deployment, and batch-size design, which counts in over-the-air FL.
q5_support: p. 13: "sense the training samples from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and KMNIST datasets"; p. 6: "Please refer to Appendix A, available in our online supplemental material". Only learning-task datasets (also CIFAR-100, p. 15), which do not count; the footnote link holds proofs, not code or channel data.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI (p. 1: "Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TVT.2025.3559147"). Eligibility: over-the-air FL passes no_learning because the learned element is the FL model; the JSCC design itself is classical optimization (AO, strategic game, QCQP, SCA, sum-of-ratios; pp. 2, 15). Aggregation is analog over the air (p. 1: "exchange model-updates with AAVs employing analog transmission scheme"; p. 5: "each AAV k aggregates the uploaded models by applying a denoising factor"), so area 7, which wins over area 6 (AAV aerial links, power control) and area 5 (ISAC sensing devices) by the specificity order. 'JSCC' in this paper means joint sensing, communication, and computation, not joint source-channel coding. SYSTEM CHECK, for the reviewer to confirm: AAVs and devices have scalar single-antenna channels (p. 4, eq. (4) and Table II 'Channel magnitude'; p. 5, eqs. (6)-(7) with a scalar denoising factor) and there is no RIS. I applied 'OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links' because all links are aerial AAV-to-ground links, which the protocol counts as NTN (area 6: satellite and aerial links; p. 3: "Since the terrestrial BS fails to offer flexible coverage for pervasive FL tasks, we concentrate on the model training performed by AAVs"). If that exception is read as limited to works assigned to areas 4 and 6, this work (area 7, single antenna, no RIS) would instead be excluded with reason system (pp. 4-5). q3: equal power transmission (fixed power configuration) is taken as the non-learned baseline; truncated channel inversion as in [22] and round-unaware error minimization solved by the scheme of [9] are earlier published aggregation designs (learned baseline under the over-the-air FL rule); static AAV is an ablation of the proposed design and error-free FedAvg an ideal bound. Carrier frequency is not given (Table III, p. 11).
